City Council Votes to Turn Parking Lot Into a Night Market

The 7-2 vote ends a two-year fight over the empty lot behind the old bus depot.

By Priya Raman

July 21, 2026

For most of the last decade, the asphalt lot behind the old Eastgate bus depot has been used for two things: storing broken traffic cones and teaching teenagers to parallel park. On Tuesday night, after a meeting that ran past eleven, the City Council voted to give it a third purpose.

Beginning next spring, the lot will host a night market three evenings a week, with space for up to sixty food and craft stalls. The plan, which passed 7 to 2, sets aside a quarter of those stalls for vendors who live within a mile of the depot, and caps stall fees for the first year.

Supporters, many of whom brought folding chairs and homemade signs, argued that the market would bring foot traffic to a stretch of Eastgate Avenue that empties out after the shops close. “People keep asking for somewhere to go in the evening that isn’t a bar,” said Ana Flores, who runs a bakery two blocks away. “This is that place.”

Opponents worried mainly about noise and parking. Councilmember Dale Hutchins, who voted against the plan, said residents of the apartment buildings that back onto the lot had not been consulted early enough. “I am not against fun,” he said. “I am against finding out about fun from a flyer.”

Advertisement

What happens next

The council directed city staff to draw up a noise plan before the first market opens, including an earlier closing time on Sundays. A small portion of the lot will be repainted as short-term parking for vendors, and the city will run a free shuttle from the Eastgate train station on market nights for the first six months.

The first vendor applications are expected to open in January. The city has not yet chosen a name for the market; a suggestion box, Ms. Flores noted, was already full of them by the end of the meeting.

A version of this article appears in print on July 22, 2026, Section A, Page 18 of the New York edition with the headline: Council Approves Eastgate Night Market.
